parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room constraint, the need to reproduce the compiled direnv-like binary from docs and behavior, and the need to avoid source lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and integration ownership while spawning docs and CLI probes, with a nested hook probe contributing shell-format behavior.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a Go replacement with main.go, config.go, env.go, eval.go, fetchurl.go, stdlib.sh, go.mod, and compile.sh, using child findings to broaden command coverage.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated code in one shared workspace, fixed post-merge build errors, rebuilt ./executable through compile.sh, and delivered the Go source tree plus executable.
parallel.verification: Used direct binary probes, child-returned behavior reports, Go builds, and smoke tests for help/version, hooks, export states, dump/apply_dump, fetchurl, and require_allowed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 763/973, so hidden behavior remained incomplete; the visible coordination issue was a shared-source edit collision that caused a build failure before final repair.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reimplementation task and relied on direct binary behavior and bundled docs without using subagents.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, cleanup, and final delivery throughout the run.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Python CLI in src/direnv.py with src/stdlib_template.sh, compile.sh, and an installed executable produced from that source.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the executable from the Python source, fixed syntax, .env suffix, and config parsing bugs, then cleaned probes so only the implementation assets remained.
serial.verification: Ran representative smoke tests for help/version, blocked and allowed .envrc loads, re-entry, unload, reload, exec, .env loading, and require_allowed approval flow.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 700/973, indicating remaining behavioral gaps despite the cleaner single-owner workflow and successful smoke tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the reverse-engineering and no-source constraints and probed docs and executable behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task and clean-room constraints from the identical prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly aligned; parallel gathered more delegated behavioral detail, while serial kept discovery local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned docs_probe and cli_probe, then later had a nested hook probe; the parent still owned final implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and one agent owned probing, implementation, fixes, build, and finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed discovery but not final ownership, whereas serial kept all work in one control loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received detailed child handoffs for CLI/private commands and hook/export behavior, and the parent inspected list_agents near closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent handoff interface; its context stayed in one agent's observations and local plan updates.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel benefited from returned probe summaries but also exposed shared-file coordination boundaries; serial avoided cross-agent context transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a Go codebase and explicitly added core source files, then finalized with modules for CLI, state, eval, fetchurl, and stdlib.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a Python implementation with a stdlib template and a shell build script that installs the Python executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel chose a compiled Go implementation with broader named modules; serial chose a Python script-based executable with a bundled template.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved completed CLI and hook probe results and saw docs_probe interrupted near closure after useful work had already been integrated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it completed local plan stages and produced one final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had multiple child results and one interrupted child chain, but no retained missing-join pattern; serial had no join risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had live actors patching shared Go source, including eval.go, and the parent observed a build failure from mismatched eval interfaces before fixing it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial edited a single Python source tree under one actor, installed it through compile.sh, and had no cross-agent write conflict.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel had a same-file collision and reconciliation episode in shared implementation state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built successfully after fixes and reported smoke tests over help/version, hooks, env states, dump/apply_dump, fetchurl, and require_allowed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built successfully and reported smoke tests over help/version, envrc loads, re-entry, unload, reload, exec, .env loading, and require_allowed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified representative behavior and both still failed the hidden official suite; parallel's stated verification covered more command categories.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout after more tool calls and four raw rollouts, interrupted one docs child late, and closed after parent-owned delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout in one raw rollout after fixing local bugs, cleaning probes, and delivering the Python build assets.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget on fan-out and reconciliation but still finalized; serial had simpler closure but lower official coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official pass/fail outcome: both current completed status evaluations have solution_passed=false. Parallel scored higher, 763/973 versus serial's 700/973, and its final response plus child reports show broader explicit coverage of fetchurl, dump/apply_dump, hook, private watch/current, and require_allowed behavior. That score gap is a concrete task-solving difference, but it does not prove a coordination error caused a pass/fail divergence. The retained parallel issue is an adverse integration process episode: same-file shared-source edits produced a build failure and repair cycle before the final compile.
parallel_contributors: Executed child probes returned detailed CLI, private command, hook, export, and required-file behavior that the parent could incorporate.
The parent delivered a Go implementation with explicit fetchurl, dump/apply_dump, hook, stdlib, and env-state smoke testing.
Concurrent same-file edits forced a build-failure reconciliation before final delivery.
serial_contributors: The serial run avoided cross-agent coordination by keeping probing, implementation, and delivery under one owner.
The serial final verification emphasized representative core env flows but did not claim exhaustive hidden-suite coverage.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a modular Go codebase; serial used a Python CLI plus bundled stdlib template.
Serial fixed ordinary implementation bugs around Python suffix handling and config parsing; parallel fixed ordinary Go compile and eval-interface mismatches.
Both retained ordinary hidden-behavior gaps because neither passed the official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both_fail; supported comparison of process and coverage, not an outcome-differential root cause
